title: Kernel generation on the source before support extension
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a commutative condensed ring $\Lambda$. Assume $\Lambda$ is isomorphic as a commutative condensed ring to one of $P\mapsto C(P,A)$ for a finite discrete commutative ring A killed by a power of ell, $P\mapsto C(P,\mathbf Z_\ell)$, $P\mapsto C(P,\mathcal O_E)$, $P\mapsto C(P,\mathbf Q_\ell)$, or $P\mapsto C(P,E)$, where $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is a finite subextension of the fixed algebraic closure, with its ell-adic topology and its ring of integers with the induced topology [sk-def-localizing-closure]. These are all continuous functions. Let S be a qcqs scheme. Let L and M be modules over $\Lambda_S=p_S^*\Lambda$ on its small pro-etale site, with ordinary uncompleted derived categories. Each is a finite scalar local model: on its own pro-etale cover it is pulled back from a finitely presented module over the condensed point [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. For every actual module morphism $f:L\to M$, the actual abelian kernel in degree zero belongs to the explicit supported image-generation hull $\mathcal G_S$ [def-sfb-supported-image-generation-hull]. There is no support extension in this assertion. Morphisms may have arbitrary continuous entries; no finite local model for the kernel is claimed. Zero maps, identity maps, zero rings and empty schemes are included.

proof.text: Let S be the given qcqs source and K = ker(u:L -> M). Refine the two finite scalar model covers to a common cover and then by weakly contractible affines, using sk-thm-pe-weakly-contractible-basis. On each resulting chart b_i:W_i -> S the restrictions of L and M are scalar models for fixed finitely presented scalar modules B_i,C_i.

proof.text: Fix one such $W$ and put $P=\pi_0(W)$. Use the component morphism $\pi_W$ and its exact fully faithful derived inverse image $F_W$. The two scalar models on $W$ are $F_W(B_R),F_W(C_R)$: present $B,C$ by finite scalar matrices; exact inverse image takes their cokernels to the cokernels of the same matrices over $\Lambda_W$. Full faithfulness gives a unique map $v:B_R\to C_R$ pulling back to $u|_W$. Degree-zero maps in a module-derived category are the module maps, so $v$ is an actual module morphism. Exactness gives $b^*K\cong F_W\ker v$. In particular we have not replaced the continuous entries of $u$ by constant entries.

proof.text: The functor $F_W$ preserves sheaf products: at a weakly contractible affine $U\to W$, its evaluation formula is $F_WM(U)=M(\pi_0U)$, and all sheaf limits are sectionwise, so the product comparison is a bijection there. The conservative basis test makes it an isomorphism. For complexes $T_j$ on $\operatorname{Prof}/P$, therefore, $F_WQ(\prod_jT_j)=Q(\prod_jF_WT_j)$. The termwise-product theorem on $W$ identifies the latter with $\prod_jF_WQT_j$ in the target derived category. Full faithfulness of $F_W$ now gives, for every source object $A$, $\operatorname{Hom}(A,Q\prod_jT_j)=\prod_j\operatorname{Hom}(A,QT_j)$. Thus $Q\prod_jT_j$ is the source derived product and $F_W$ carries it to the target derived product. Also $F_W$ preserves termwise filtered colimits, as an inverse-image left adjoint; it is exact and hence sends a strict diagram with common termwise lower bound to one with that same bound. Exactness preserves shifts and triangles, and any functor preserves retract diagrams.

proof.text: Every generator of $\mathcal H_P$ pulls back to a finite scalar local model on $W$: the component site functor carries its covering to a pro-étale covering, and the scalar cokernel calculation of step 2 applies on its members. Consequently $\{T:F_WT\in\mathcal G_W\}$ is one of the full replete classes intersected to define $\mathcal H_P$, by step 3 and by the identity-chain generators of $\mathcal G_W$. It contains $\mathcal H_P$. The profinite relation-kernel lemma applies to $v$ and yields $(\ker v)[0]\in\mathcal H_P$. Thus $(b^*K)[0]\in\mathcal G_W$ for every chart $W$.

proof.text: Apply supported-hull pro-étale descent to the module $K$ on the qcqs scheme $S$ and the cover chosen in step 1. The hypothesis of that lemma was proved in step 4, so $K[0]\in\mathcal G_S$. This is descent of membership in the specified hull; it is not inferred merely from conservativity of restriction or descent of lisse sheaves.

lean.statement: theorem finite_model_kernel_mem_supported_generation (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (hΛ : (∃ (A : Type) (_ : CommRing A) (_ : TopologicalSpace A) (_ : DiscreteTopology A) (_ : IsTopologicalRing A), Finite A ∧ (∃ n : ℕ, ∀ a : A, (ℓ ^ n) • a = 0) ∧ Nonempty (Mon.mk Λ ≅ Mon.mk (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj A))) ∨ Nonempty (Mon.mk Λ ≅ Mon.mk (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj ℤ_[ℓ])) ∨ (∃ E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField ℓ, Nonempty (Mon.mk Λ ≅ Mon.mk (Profinite.padicIntegersRingObj ℓ E))) ∨ Nonempty (Mon.mk Λ ≅ Mon.mk (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj ℚ_[ℓ])) ∨ (∃ E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField ℓ, Nonempty (Mon.mk Λ ≅ Mon.mk (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj E)))) (S : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] (L M : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology S) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ S)) (hL : HasFiniteConstantLocalModel Λ S L) (hM : HasFiniteConstantLocalModel Λ S M) (f : L ⟶ M) : supportedImageGenerationHull Λ S ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj (kernel f))
